summary:
The Cephalonia massacre was a major German war crime against Italian prisoners of war in September 1943. After Italy’s armistice with the Allies, the Acqui Division resisted German efforts to disarm it on the Greek island of Cephalonia. The fighting ended on 22 September, when the Italians surrendered after running out of ammunition.

German troops executed about 5,155 Italian soldiers, including General Antonio Gandin and other officers. Many bodies were burned or thrown into the sea. About 3,000 other Italian prisoners drowned when ships carrying them to camps were sunk by Allied attacks and mines. The massacre followed orders permitting the summary execution of Italian officers who had resisted. It was one of the largest prisoner-of-war massacres of the Second World War.
